Description: A hollow ball with a pinhole: a ball of radius 20 with a concentric spherical cavity of radius 12, and a bore of radius 2 from the cavity out through the wall along +z. The cavity is therefore not a cavity yet - the body has one single connected boundary. Growing by 3 has to close the bore, because the wall grows 3 from every side while the bore is only 2 wide, so the cavity becomes a real one and the result must be a hollow ball again. Shrinking by 3 is the counter-test: the wall thins from 8 to 2 and the bore widens, so the body stays a single open surface.
Expected: hollowBall is exact: V = 4/3*pi*(20^3-12^3) = 26272.0922, A = 4*pi*(400+144) = 6836.1056, two spherical faces and euler 4 - two closed components, the hull and the cavity. pinholed joins the two spheres through the bore, so it is ONE component: euler 2, with a cylindrical face for the bore. The point of the case is pinholeGrown: closed, consistent, and euler 4 again, the cavity back as a component of its own. Its volume is a little below 4/3*pi*(23^3-9^3) = 47911.3824, because the cavity keeps a small bulge along the bore axis: the nearest material to an axis point is the rim of the hole in the cavity wall, at sqrt(2^2+(12-t)^2) instead of 12-t, so the cavity reaches to t = 12-sqrt(3^2-2^2) = 9.7639 rather than 9. pinholeShrunk must stay one component (euler 2), outer radius 17, cavity radius 15, and therefore clearly below 4/3*pi*(17^3-15^3) = 6442.3593, since the bore, now 5 wide, takes a bite out of the 2 mm wall that is left.
Status: PASSES (2026-09-11). Keep as a regression guard for the topology change an offset can cause: growing turns a body with one single boundary into one with a real cavity. Written while that did not work at all - see Actual for the three stages it went through.

pinholeGrown.verified: 2026-09-11 THE POINT OF THIS CASE: growing by 3 closes the 2 mm bore, so the cavity becomes a cavity again - euler 4, closed and consistent, against euler 2 of the input. The four faces say exactly how: two spheres (hull 23, cavity 9) and two TORI. A torus is what the dilation of a circle is, and the two hole rims are circles of radius 2 - one on the outer sphere, one on the cavity sphere - so each grows into a torus of tube radius 3. The extent confirms it: max z = 19.8997+3 = 22.8997 instead of 23, the hull is not a full sphere but carries the toroidal cap where the bore used to be. The volume 47913.5936 sits 4.6e-5 above the plain sphere difference 4/3*pi*(23^3-9^3) = 47911.3824; the two geometric corrections (the cavity keeps a bulge along the bore axis, the hull is flattened at the cap) both point down by a few units, the mesh bias of the spherical faces points up by about as much, so the volume cannot separate them at this precision - the topology is the decisive check here.
